nodes.name: 银鳞落
nodes.light: low gold of a late-autumn evening from the right across the water, with the cool grey-blue of the lake and of the shadows behind
nodes.camera: at the height of the cooking fire, looking across it at the boy's face with the old man large behind him; a little tilted
nodes.text: Scene: evening on the east shore of a still forest lake, so flat that it holds the sky and a single ancient tree whose branches trail in the water. In the near middle, a small cooking fire of driftwood burns on a flat stone, and over it on a rack of green twigs lies a whole fish roasted brown. The fish's skin was silver, and the silver is going out of it as we look: a last film of shining scales is lifting off the roasted skin like breath off glass, a glitter drifting up into the smoke. Crouched at the fire in the left half of the picture is a slender boy of seventeen, long snow-white hair tied at the nape with a plain leather cord, a small teardrop mole under his right eye (on the viewer's left), a thin healed scar between his brows, a fish-skin pouch at his belt; he has his thumb in his mouth and his head raised, and in his lake-grey-blue eyes there is one flash of silver, wide and startled, looking at nothing, at everything. Behind him and to the right, stooped and tall, an old poet with a long white beard to his chest and a thin growth of white hair held back by a reed holds a wooden platter out in both hands, pushing it toward the boy, his bright eyes squeezed to slits in a wide smile, tears in them. A fishing rod with a bare hook leans against his shoulder. Behind them the fishing nets are drying on poles and a reed-thatched hut stands on the shore, with birch-bark strips of songs hung under its eaves. A flight of geese crosses the sky. Drifting woodsmoke, a falling leaf and a few glittering scales float large and out of focus across the corners.

nodes.name: 门边的矛
nodes.light: the warm orange of torches and a great hearth spilling out of the hall doorway behind him, against the cold blue of the night outside
nodes.camera: from outside the hall door at the boy's shoulder, looking past him at the old soldier in the doorway; a little tilted
nodes.text: Scene: night at the great hall of a hill-fortress, just outside its tall oak doors, which stand open. From inside comes the red-gold light of torches and a long hearth, and the dim shapes of a crowd at a harvest feast, bearded kings' envoys and hunters round long tables, still laughing. In the near left foreground, seen from behind at three-quarter so that we see one cheek and one lake-grey eye, stands a slender white-haired boy of seventeen, hair tied at the nape with a leather cord, a fish-skin pouch at his belt; he has just walked out of the hall and his shoulders are set, his face pale and fixed, not laughing. In front of him, sitting on a stone bench against the doorpost, is a stranger, an old soldier in a worn grey cloak, a plain man's face half in shadow, his long spear held out horizontally across both palms toward the boy. The spear is long and plain, its shaft glittering with white hoar frost from the butt to the grey blade, and the frost does not melt although the torchlight pours on it and a drift of warm hall air rolls across it. The old man says one quiet word and does not smile. Rime has also crept along the stone sill and the old man's fingertips. Further back in the hall doorway a one-eyed, iron-grey, broad-shouldered hunter-chief with a bear-hide patch sits at a king's left hand, laughing loudest, with a notched silver staff leaning on his chair. Overhead a few cold stars show over the dark hill, and drifting sparks from the hall's torches and a few big out-of-focus flakes of frost glitter across the near corners.

nodes.name: 第七个孔
who: the white-haired boy with the spear
nodes.light: blazing orange-red fire from the beast on the gate tower above, against the pale cold blue of the spear's ice and a deep blue night
nodes.camera: very low at the foot of the gate, looking up the arch at the beast on the tower, the boy's silhouette at the lower left; strongly tilted
nodes.text: Scene: night at the burnt gate of a hill-city. A colossal fire-lizard sits on top of the gate tower, much bigger than the gate: a lizard's long body and head, but on its back are two vast burning wing-membranes, red and glowing, spread wide enough to cover half a city and cut off by the top of the frame. Its long throat is pierced with seven round holes like the holes of a pipe, each one glowing white-hot, and flame rolls from its open mouth. Its fire is not reaching the ground: just below its throat, at the seventh hole, a long ice-white spear has struck dead centre and is buried to the shaft, and from that point cold blue shards of ice are bursting outward in a huge star, scattering and cooling the flames around them into drifting frost. Below, in the near left, small against the arch of the gate, stands a slender white-haired boy of seventeen, long hair tied at the nape, a fish-skin pouch at his belt, seen from below and behind at three-quarter so that we see one cheek: his right arm is still thrown forward and extended at the end of the throw, his body twisted, his eyes wide and clear and awake, his mouth set. Along the walls and the gate towers all the city's guards have fallen asleep where they stand, slumped on their spears; a one-eyed hunter-chief lies against a doorpost asleep, and a lean grey-haired huntress with a longbow sleeps against the wall's foot, still clutching the bow. The whole town is silent beneath the red sky. Ice shards, sparks and falling ash glitter large and out of focus across the corners.

nodes.name: 火边一席
who: the white-haired captain of the nine spears
nodes.light: the warm gold of a campfire and a low autumn sunrise behind the walls, against the blue-grey of the plain
nodes.camera: at the height of the fire, looking across it past the hunters at the burnt gate behind them; a little tilted
nodes.text: Scene: dawn on the plain outside a white hill-city, in the first days of winter. Behind, filling the upper background, the white stone wall climbs the hill, and in its great gate there is one wide scorched black patch where nobody has repaired the stonework, so the dark scar is clear against the pale stone. In the middle of the picture a campfire burns before the wall, and about twenty hunters sit and stand round it: men and women in deerskin and grey-green cloaks, long spears planted in the earth beside them, a few with beast ears, one a weaver's daughter with a bow. Seated on a log at the fire's right side is a slender young man of seventeen, long snow-white hair tied at the nape, a fish-skin pouch at his belt, a long silver-grey staff with a notch at its head across his knees, his lake-grey eyes quiet and tired; the staff's shaft is carved with small marks. A one-eyed, iron-grey, broad-shouldered older hunter with a black bear-hide patch stands just behind him, a spear in his hand, his hawk-gold eye on the fire, looking at the boy's back with a stern, unreadable face. At the fire's left side the hunters have shifted along the log, leaving one place empty, and a thin tired woman with a baby in a shawl, a stranger, is just about to step into the gap, her face wet with relief. Along the far wall a few women are carrying children indoors, singing. Woodsmoke, drifting ash and a few big out-of-focus snow-flakes catch the gold light across the near corners.

芬尼.how: 那个冬天他把白丘那一夜编成了歌，是头一首唱九矛的歌。开春他死在湖边，手里还攥着钓竿，竿上什么也没有。

戈尔.where: 平原上，一头熔角犀的群首跟前
戈尔.how: 九矛在平原上围一头冲进麦田的熔角犀群首，那东西转过头冲向席恩，他抢在前头，一矛扎进了它的眼睛，它的角也扎穿了他。死前那一下，他的矛跑在了席恩的矛前头。他死的时候六十二岁。

notes: deaths 里黎丝死在约1388年（74岁），在这一歌主线年份（1350）以外，我照旅伴条的正史下场写了；她的年份是按年龄推的，源稿没写，请定。
戈尔1366年的死很有画面，可他在任务单里是相遇不是旅伴，所以没有死的那一刻，只写了 fates，要不要加一幅请定。
席恩17岁，n3 里没画眉心的血痕，只画他掷出矛的那一下；n1 的拇指也没画烫伤。
n4 里黎丝没入画（她做守考人那一拍太散），改画戈尔站在席恩身后，请审戈尔这时的神情是不是对。
伯德玛的年龄任务单写52岁，下场写81岁死在1381年，对不上，我只照源稿写了1381年冬天。

柯马.how: 天亮以后他把那根银杖还给了少年，又把猎团交给了他。往后二十一年他做他的王，白丘秋收以后不再挨烧，城门上那一片焦黑他留着，不许人修。

伯德玛.where: 林海深处的老橡树底下
伯德玛.how: 她回了林海深处，守着火，看梦，活到八十一岁。那一根枝子烧出来的是什么，她到死也没对席恩说。有人说，她看见的是一双手，捧着水，水从指缝里漏下去。

黎丝.how: 她做了九矛的守考人，三十多年里每一个想进九矛的人，都要先跟着她在林子里跑一趟，踩断一根枯枝的，她就叫他回去。她死在七十四岁那年冬天，死在林子里。

later_deaths.name: 无声的林
later_deaths.light: the cold pale blue of a winter forenoon filtering down through bare branches, with one shaft of thin gold light falling on her
later_deaths.camera: at the height of the deer's eyes, looking along the forest floor at her from the front; a slight tilt
later_deaths.text: Scene: the deep of an old forest in winter, tall bare trunks rising on all sides into a pale sky, the ground under a deep soft snow with a few brown leaves lying on it. In the middle of the picture an old huntress of seventy-four stands upright, her left hand resting on the trunk of a huge oak and her longbow in her right hand, held low. She is tall and lean still, and her short hair is white, with one long lock across her forehead covering an old scar at the outer corner of her right eye (on the viewer's left); a long dark wool cloak and deerskin leggings; her face is thin, finely lined, cold and beautiful, with her forest-green eyes open and fixed on something ahead of her, and a very small, girlish smile at the corner of her mouth. A single white hair, a child's, is wound round the back of the bow. She is quite still. There is no mark in the snow round her feet but one line of her own prints, and not a twig has been broken: the snow in her footsteps is barely dented. Ahead of her, a few paces off, a young deer stands in the open with its head raised, looking back at her with its ears forward, unafraid. Behind her, far away between the trunks, a few figures in cloaks, young hunters who have followed her, stand watching quietly. Falling snow crystals and drifting wisps of breath-mist glitter large and out of focus across the near corners.
